schema.description: List Claude Code Remote sessions visible to the authenticated account. In bot contexts (e.g. Slack) this is a shared pool spanning many people, not just the human asking — pass mine: true to narrow to sessions started by the same account as the calling session. Returns session IDs, titles, statuses, and timestamps.

after_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions older than this session ID. Pass the last_id from a previous response to get the next page.

before_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions newer than this session ID. Pass the first_id from a previous response to get the previous page.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (default 20, max 100).

mine.description: Filter to sessions started by the same account as the calling session. Use this for 'my recent sessions' in shared bot contexts. In personal accounts the list is already scoped to you, so mine has no additional effect. Returns an error if the calling session has no resolvable originating account.

tags.description: Filter to interactive sessions carrying ANY of these tags. Cowork sessions are tagged "cowork-local" or "cowork-remote" and are excluded from the default (untagged) listing — pass those tags here to list them. Scheduled/trigger-fired runs are not included (same as the REST default). Max 16 tags. Only available to OAuth callers; returns an error for in-session and toolbox callers.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
schema.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

all_in_channel.description: Threads in a Slack channel only. If true, list every Routine in this channel, including other threads' and ones that start a new session each time they fire. Default false.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

enabled.description: When set, only Routines whose enabled state matches. true hides fired one-shots, paused, and auto-disabled Routines; false shows only those. Omit for both.

include_completed.description: If true, also include one-shot Routines that have already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project. Default false — there can be thousands.

recurring.description: When set, filters by schedule shape: true keeps only cron-driven (recurring) Routines, false only one-shot and fire-only Routines. Omit for both.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__read_documentation
tools.description: The documentation for the machine and product this session runs in: a claude.ai cloud container and the settings around it (GitHub access, connectors, the environment's secrets, network access, setup script and installed tools, the session's limits, Remote Control). Read it whenever something about your container or environment comes up, whether it blocked you, you worked around it, or the person asked how to set it up. For example: a clone or push is refused, a service you need has no connected connector, an outbound host is denied, a command-line tool is missing, you need an API key. Read it rather than answering from memory because these settings move and get renamed faster than your training data, and a page says what is true now: the current steps, where in the product the person makes the change, and what you can do yourself. Reading a page also helps the person directly: in the Claude Code app they see a card with a button that takes them to that settings page, so they can fix it themselves while you carry on. Call it with no topic to list the pages and when each applies; call it with a topic to read that page. Read a page each time a different topic comes up; one read per topic is enough. It is read-only and needs no approval. It has nothing on bugs in the code you are working on.

service.description: The product the topic came up for, when there is one: must be one of this field's enum values. "other" stands for any product that is not among them. Omit it when no product is involved.

situation.description: Why you are reading the page. "blocked": you cannot finish what was asked. "worked_around": you finished another way. "asked": the person asked how to set this up, or you can see it will be needed.

topic.description: The page to read. Must be one of this field's enum values. Omit it to get the index of pages.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__register_repo_root
tools.description: Tell the session that a repo attached via add_repo has finished cloning, so its CLAUDE.md, skills, and plugins load on the next turn. Only call this immediately after a successful clone that add_repo instructed you to run — it returns a tool error for a repo that is not already in this session's sources.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__register_repo_root
schema.description: Tell the session that a repo attached via add_repo has finished cloning, so its CLAUDE.md, skills, and plugins load on the next turn. ## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

### 4.3 The fixed widths, and how the count is read

Each of the four shift pairs gains one line before the existing one; `Int$LShift` (`Int.java:180-185`), for example, is `if (v < 0) return (v > -32) ? (u >> (int) -v) : (u >> 31);` followed by the original `((v & ~31) == 0) ? (u << (int) v) : 0`. The comparison with `-32` (`-64`) precedes the negation, so `Long.MIN_VALUE` is never negated. `NN32` and `NN64` shift right logically and saturate to `0` both ways (`NN32.java:183-195`, `UnsignedLong.java:184-196`).

**The `NN64` question, established.** `UnsignedLong$LShift` took its count through `UU2U`, whose `applyMethod` reads `y.getNN64()` (base `UnsignedLong.java:88-94`). Through that `long`, a negative count and a large unsigned one cannot be told apart: `FInt.getNN64` and `FLong.getNN64` return the signed value unchanged (`evaluator/values/FInt.java:36-39`, `FLong.java:37-40`), so a `ZZ32` count of `-1` and an `NN64` count of `2^64-1` both arrive as `-1L`, and `Long.MIN_VALUE` as a `ZZ64` count and `2^63` as an `NN64` count both arrive as `Long.MIN_VALUE`. **They can be told apart one step earlier, by the class of the count's value**, which is `FNN64` for an `NN64`. The same ambiguity sat in `Long$…` (`y.getLong()` of an `FNN64` is its raw bits) and in `BigNum`'s `ZL2Z`; it was harmless while every negative count saturated, and this rung's negative-count rule would have made it wrong (`-3 LSHIFT` an `NN64` count of `2^63` would have become a right shift, `-1` instead of `0`). So the count is read once, by `Int.shiftCount(FValue)` (`Int.java:261-272`): an `FNN64` of `2^63` or more as `Long.MAX_VALUE` (a count beyond every width), an `FBigNum` exactly when it fits a `long` and clamped to `Long.MIN_VALUE`/`Long.MAX_VALUE` when it does not (exact for every width, and for `ZZ`, whose values the JVM limits to `2^31-1` bits), anything else by `getLong()`. The guards are asserted at `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:73-76`.

Precedent for the shape: each natives file declares small abstract classes named for their Java types, with a shift-only one where the count's reading differs: `ZL2Z` in `Int.java:90-96` and `BigNum.java:102-108`, `NL2N` in `NN32.java:95-101`, each extended by the two shifts alone (`grep -n "extends ZL2Z\|extends NL2N"` finds only the shifts, plus the dormant `ZZ32.java`). Their `applyMethod` now calls `shiftCount`. `Long.java` and `UnsignedLong.java` had only the shared `LL2L`/`UU2U`, so each gains a shift-only twin, `LC2L` (`Long.java:104-110`) and `UC2U` (`UnsignedLong.java:96-102`), "C" for the count; the alternative, extending `NativeMeth1` directly as the `Pow` classes do (`Int.java:218-228`), was rejected to keep the four pairs one shape.

### 4.4 The unbounded ZZ

`BigNum$LShift` and `$RShift` (`BigNum.java:225-235`) call one helper, `shiftLeft(BigInteger, long)` (`BigNum.java:237-250`); `RShift` negates the count, mapping `Long.MIN_VALUE` to `Long.MAX_VALUE` first (both are beyond any `BigInteger`'s width, so the answer is the same). A negative count of magnitude up to `Integer.MAX_VALUE` is a `BigInteger.shiftRight`, a floor, as the spec's `shift` requires; beyond it the answer is `0` or `-1` by sign; zero shifted is zero; a positive count beyond `Integer.MAX_VALUE` on a nonzero value raises `IntegerOverflow`, and so does the JVM's own `ArithmeticException("BigInteger would overflow supported range")` for a count inside the `int` range whose result exceeds `BigInteger`'s limit (measured with a throwaway Java probe on JDK 25: `3 << 2147483645` succeeds with bit length `2147483647`, `3 << 2147483646` throws), caught at the call and translated.

**Decision: `IntegerOverflow`, catchable.** The brief left the exception to the rung. The alternatives were the raw `ArithmeticException` (uncatchable under `walk`, row 336's shape, and what the base tree already did for counts inside the `int` range), a `ProgramError` through `error(...)` (uncatchable, row 347's shape), or a new exception type. The spec's rule is that an integer result that does not fit throws `IntegerOverflow` (`opr-overview.tex:154-155`); `ZZ` has no width of its own but the JVM gives it one, and Pavol's principle is not to fight the JVM where it precludes an implementation; `IntegerOverflow` is the one exception the library has for "an integer result that does not fit". Translating the JVM's own check rather than predicting it keeps the limit the JVM's.

### 4.5 ZZ64.narrow

`Long$FromLong` is `(int) x` (`Long.java:248-252`), as `UnsignedLong$FromLong` (`UnsignedLong.java:240-243`) and `BigNum$ToZZ32` (`BigNum.java:282-285`) already were.

## 5. The `shift` declaration: the collision, and the renames the specification requires

The declaration is written as the brief says: `shift(self, k:AnyIntegral): ZZ` in `trait ZZ` of `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` (`:544`), and in the component `shift(self, k:AnyIntegral): ZZ = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.BigNum$LShift")` after `RSHIFT` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:885-886`). **Alone, it collided, not with the dotted method, but with every declaration of a parameter or local named `shift` in a component that sees the library**, and every `walk` run then failed before the program started. It is not peculiar to `shift`: `probes/ShadowEven.fss` binds a parameter `even` and a local `numerator`, both functional methods of the library's `ZZ` today, and on the unedited library gets `Variable even is already declared.` and `Variable numerator is already declared.` (`probes/ShadowEven.txt`). The specification makes the collision real at least inside the library's own component: "It is also a static error for multiple declarations with overlapping reaches to declare the same name in the same namespace unless the declarations are overloaded or one declaration shadows the other" (`Specification/basic/declarations.tex:426-432`); a parameter is not among the declarations that may shadow ("No other shadowing is permitted in a Fortress program", `:533`, after the list at `:476-529`); and "The reach of a functional method declaration is the component containing that declaration" (`:435-436`), which takes in `FortressLibrary`'s own `Range` trait. A parameter's own reach is its functional declaration (`:459-461`), so the reaches overlap. For the importing components (`RangeInternals`, `List`, a user's program), "the reach of any top-level declaration (including any imported declaration) is the component containing (or importing) that declaration" (`:454-456`), which is the reading the implementation, shared by both paths, enforces.

# Judge's second ruling on rung I: the skeptic's refusal at `ecc71113a`

Invoked on the skeptic's refusal of the landed rung (`SKEPTIC.md`, commit `ecc71113a`). I read the net change (`git diff abdfbb2db...HEAD`), the eight milestones, `REPORT.md`, `record.md`, `SKEPTIC.md`, the skeptic's captures under `probes/skeptic/`, the batch record `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, the specification passages both cite with ten lines either side, and the natives and library declarations at the cited lines. I ran nothing. The worktree was clean.

The first ruling above (lines 1-87) is left byte for byte as it was, because `REPORT.md`, `record.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` cite it by section and by line; one error in it is corrected here and not edited in: line 14 cites `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:18` for Pavol's decision, and that line is blank; the decision is `:17` (section 5 below). Line numbers of this part start at 89.

**Decision: repair.** The skeptic's refusal ground stands, and so do its findings 2 to 8, each by the citations below. The repair round edits one Java file (`BigNum.java`, two sites), adds three assertions to the gated test, and rewrites the parts of `REPORT.md` and `record.md` the findings touch; it opens four ledger rows on the skeptic's measurements. The Java natives of the four fixed widths, the library declaration and the renames are not touched.

## 1. Finding 1, the refusal ground: upheld

**What is true.** `BigNum.shiftLeft` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/BigNum.java:237-250`) bounds the count at `:243` (`if (v > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw Int.overflow();`) and then calls `u.shiftLeft((int) v)` inside a `try` at `:244-249`, translating the `ArithmeticException`. The JVM's `BigInteger.shiftLeft` allocates the shifted magnitude before its range check throws, so for `3 << 2147483647` about 268 MB is asked for first. The interpreter's launcher gives the JVM `-Xmx256m` unless `JAVA_FLAGS` is set (`bin/fortress:28-29`), and the harness gives it 768 MB (root `build.xml:131`, `junitMem`, used by the `junit` task's `maxmemory` at `:1181`; `probes/harness-one.sh` copies that as `-Xmx768m`). Measured by the skeptic on the landed tree: under `bin/fortress` with `JAVA_FLAGS` unset the gated test dies at `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:93` with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap.txt:1-3`), and prints `PASS` without that line (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap-no93.txt`); the same shift is `THROWS IntegerOverflow` at 768m and 4g (`probes/skeptic/SkBigAlloc.txt:6-10`) and an `OutOfMemoryError` at 256m (`:1-4`).

**Why it is refusal-grade.** Three reasons, any one enough. `record.md` FACTS line 2 (`record.md:10`) and `REPORT.md` section 4.4 (`REPORT.md:71-73`) claim an unrepresentable left shift raises "a catchable `IntegerOverflow`", unconditionally; it does so only above the launcher's heap, and a claim that holds only under the shared prefix's `JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g ..."` is not a fact about the tree. An `OutOfMemoryError` is a `java.lang.Error` that no Fortress `catch` and no harness expected-failure sees, so the gated assertion `:93` is a red at the tree's own default that the gate cannot show. And a runtime that allocates 268 MB to learn that a shift does not fit, when the answer is one `bitLength()`, is the wrong shape for a language whose specification says overflow "throws an `IntegerOverflow`" (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-155`, read with `:140-170`).

**The repair, and why it is exact.** The skeptic's one line after `:243`, `if (u.abs().bitLength() + v > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw Int.overflow();`, trialled in a scratch overlay (`probes/skeptic/fix-trial-patch.txt`), makes the unmodified test print `PASS` at `-Xmx256m` (`probes/skeptic/fix-trial-default-heap.txt`). It is exact by the worker's own measurement in `REPORT.md:71`: `3 << 2147483645` succeeds with bit length 2147483647 and `3 << 2147483646` throws, which is `2 + 2147483645 <= Integer.MAX_VALUE < 2 + 2147483646`; the JVM's limit is a magnitude of `Integer.MAX_VALUE` bits, and `u.abs().bitLength()` is the magnitude's bit length (for a negative power of two, `u.bitLength()` alone is one less, so `abs()` is not decoration). Two things the repair worker must keep:

- `:243` stays, and stays first. `Int.shiftCount` (`Int.java:261-272`) clamps an `NN64` count of `2^63` or more and a `ZZ` count beyond a `long` to `Long.MAX_VALUE`; without `:243` ahead of it, `bitLength + v` overflows the `long`, the precheck falls through, and `(int) v` is `-1`, a silent right shift. The existing assertion `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:95` (`bigThree LSHIFT twoTo63` overflows) is the guard on that order.
- The `try`/`catch` at `:244-249` stays as a backstop. The precheck's exactness rests on a JDK-internal constant (`BigInteger.MAX_MAG_LENGTH`), which is the JDK's to change; the catch costs nothing and keeps the translation if the constant ever moves.

**What the worker got wrong here, and what right.** `REPORT.md:73` took a decision, "translating the JVM's own check rather than predicting it keeps the limit the JVM's", without measuring at the launcher's heap; the shared prefix's `JAVA_FLAGS` hid the failure, and the base tree fails the same way (the base's `u.shiftLeft((int) v)` at base `BigNum.java:224` is the same call), so this is not a regression but it is the rung's claim. Everything else in section 4.4 is right and stays: the negative count of any size, zero shifted, the count beyond `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, and the choice of `IntegerOverflow` (`opr-overview.tex:154-155`).

`ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss` covers every case the tail names: the shared table on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, the `NN32`/`NN64` reversals, the two `ZZ` counts beyond the `int` range, the three named `shift` cases, row 334's cases and twins, and the four `narrow`s. It has one comment line (`:4`), pointing at `REPORT.md`, and no provenance essay.

Under the testSystem harness, on a fresh cache, it is `OK (1 test)` (`probes/skeptic/harness-test.txt`). Two of its assertions are weaker than they look:

- **`:93`** passes only because the harness JVM has 768 MB (`build.xml:131`, `junitMem`, used by the shard macro at `:1181`). Under `bin/fortress`, whose default heap is `-Xmx256m` (`bin/fortress`, the `JAVA_FLAGS` default), the test dies with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap.txt:1-2`). The same file without `:93` prints `PASS` at that heap (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap-no93.txt:1`).
- **`:82`** (`ZZ32 -3 RSHIFT a ZZ count of 40` = -1, cited to `FortressLibrary.fss:637`) is independent of the width, because a negative number shifted right past 32 or past 64 is -1 either way. It therefore does not exercise what finding 3 measures.

## 5. Competing declarations

I searched `git grep -nw shift` over every tracked `.fss`/`.fsi` outside `Specification/`, `explorations/` and `Library/incomplete/`, excluding `.shift(` calls and comment lines. It finds:
- the new declaration and body;
- the seven array-origin dotted declarations (`FortressLibrary.fsi:1294`, `:1317`, `:1337`, `:1417`, `:1447`, `:1557`, `:1688`). `:1557`'s component body at `FortressLibrary.fss:2373` is inside `trait Array2` (`:2295`);
- the dead `CompilerLibrary/FortressLibrary.fsi` group, including `:2061-2064`;
- comments and strings;
- this rung's own calls.

Under `src/com/sun/fortress/`, `"shift"` occurs nowhere, `"IntegerOverflow"` and `integerOverflowException` occur only at `WellKnownNames.java:86` and `Int.java:257`, and `shiftCount`, `LC2L` and `UC2U` occur only in the five natives files.

The reserved name is real for user programs. On the landed tree, a local and a parameter named `shift` are rejected under `walk` with `Variable shift is already declared.` and accepted on the compiled path (`SkShiftLocal.*.txt`, `SkShiftParam.*.txt`). A user top-level function named `shift` of either shape overloads cleanly on both paths (`SkShiftFn.*.txt`, `SkShiftFn2.*.txt`).

## 6. `record.md`

The FACTS lines are sourced, and I confirmed the counts they state:
- 25 `overflows(...)` assertions;
- 52 assertions at `:29-95`, 7 at `:97-103`, 31 at `:105-139` and 4 at `:141-145`;
- `Int.rc`'s callers `Int.java:152` and `:225`;
- the row 347 correction (`ZZ32.java:208` and `NN32.java:226` call their own `rc`, declared at `ZZ32.java:225` and `NN32.java:257`).

Rows 334, 335, 336, 346 and 347 exist (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:345-358`), and nothing is renumbered. Three statements are not true as written:
- FACTS line 2 says "an unrepresentable left shift a catchable `IntegerOverflow`". That is false at the launcher's default heap (finding 1).
- The row 334 note closes the row while the unbounded ℤ's `LCM` still returns `1 LCM -5` = -5 (finding 2).
- FACTS line 2 says of the `ZZ` count only that it "is read exactly". It does not say what a `ZZ32` receiver then answers (finding 3).

## 7. The three homes

The worker's homes are in place and pass (I ran the test): `:29-95`, `:97-103` (the seventh assertion at `:103` included), `:105-139`, `:141-145`, `:81-82` and `:94-96`/`:101`. The `XXXShiftRungI.fss` placeholder was removed before it ever reached `main`, and its deliberate-red capture stays committed. The `RangeInternals.fss` tuple defects are unmeasured, and I did not measure them either.

Each defect I measured has a home:
- **Finding 1**: home 1, after the repair round. The assertion `:93` already exists, and it must then pass under `bin/fortress` at the default heap.
- **Finding 2**: home 1 (repair plus assertions) or home 2 (an `XXX` file, with row 334 left open for ℤ). The specification settles it (`basic-integers.tex:527-529`).
- **Finding 3**: home 3. The specification's prose is silent on `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` (the worker's own `grep -rn "LSHIFT\|RSHIFT\|narrow" Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` matches nothing), and the repair is a batch stop. My captures are committed, and a row is recommended below.
- **Findings 6-8**: compiled-path defects, outside this rung. Each is in `recommendedRows`.

## 8. The count table

The table is `probes/checker-count-after-shift.txt`, `#total 103`, byte-identical to `probes/checker-count-before.txt`. The report declares 103 (`REPORT.md:120`), `record.md`'s handover line says "stays 103", and the structured report says "The checker count is 103". The manifest's `expectedCheckerCount` is 103, a prediction. Table 103, report 103, prediction 103: no mismatch.

## 10. The failure-mode question

These are the loud failures the rung turned into values, and what each value is:
- **`0 LCM 0`**: a raw `ArithmeticException` becomes 0. This is the specification's answer (`basic-integers.tex:529`).
- **Out-of-range `ZZ64.narrow`**: a `ProgramError` becomes the low 32 bits. This is Pavol's decision; the specification is silent.
- **A `ZZ` count on a fixed-width shift**: `ProgramError: Value 33 might not fit in ZZ64.` becomes a value. On a `ZZ64` receiver the value is right. On a `ZZ32` receiver it is the `ZZ64` method's 64-bit answer, typed `ZZ64`: `3 LSHIFT big(33)` = 25769803776 and `3 LSHIFT big(40)` = 3298534883328, where the shared table's rule for a `ZZ32` gives 0. That is finding 3, and the report does not state it.
- **A `ZZ` shift whose result the JVM cannot hold**: at 768 MB and above, a raw `ArithmeticException` becomes a catchable `IntegerOverflow`. At the launcher's default 256 MB it is still an `OutOfMemoryError`, as on the base tree (finding 1).

In the other direction, the rung makes previously valid `walk` programs that bind `shift` a static error. The specification requires that, and the corpus has no such program.

## 11. Findings

1. **(The refusal.)** At the interpreter's default heap, an unrepresentable `ZZ` left shift with a count inside the `int` range is an uncatchable `OutOfMemoryError`, not `IntegerOverflow`, and the rung's gated test dies at `:93`.
   - Cause: `BigNum.shiftLeft` calls `u.shiftLeft((int) v)` (`BigNum.java:245`) and translates only the `ArithmeticException` that `BigInteger` raises after it has allocated the magnitude array. For `3 << 2147483647` that array is about 268 MB.
   - Evidence: `test-default-heap.txt` (red), `test-default-heap-no93.txt` (`PASS` without `:93`), `SkBigAlloc.txt`.
   - Repair: one line after `:243`, `if (u.abs().bitLength() + v > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw Int.overflow();`. `BigInteger` holds magnitudes up to 2^31-1 bits, so the test is exact, and the `catch` stays as a backstop. I applied it in a scratch class overlay only, not to the tree (`fix-trial-patch.txt`), and the unmodified test printed `PASS` at `-Xmx256m` (`fix-trial-default-heap.txt`).
   - This is not a regression (the base tree also runs out of memory at 256 MB), but the rung's claim and its gated assertion hold only at the harness heap.
2. **The unbounded ℤ's `LCM` keeps row 334's defect.** Under `walk`, `big(1) LCM big(-5)` = -5, `big(-4) LCM big(6)` = -12, and `big(0) LCM big(0)` ends the run with `ArithmeticException: BigInteger divide by zero` (`SkBigLcm.walk.txt`).
   - Location: `BigNum$Lcm`, `BigNum.java:176-188`, bound at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:871-872`, in a file the rung already edits.
   - Settled by `basic-integers.tex:527-529`. That section declares `LCM` on ℤ itself (`:521`).
   - Consequences: the report's site count misses it (`REPORT.md:128`), and the row 334 note cannot say "close" while this stands.
3. **Under `walk`, a `ZZ32` receiver shifted by a count that is not a `ZZ64` (`ZZ`, `NN32`, `NN64`) is computed at width 64 and answered as a `ZZ64`.**
   - Cause: `ZZ32`'s own `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` declare `b:ZZ64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:688-691`), so any other count type dispatches to `ZZ64`'s `b:AnyIntegral` pair (`:756-759`, `Long$LShift`), although `Integral[\I\]` declares `opr LSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):I` (`:637-638`).
   - Before and after: the `NN` counts gave this answer before the rung, while the `ZZ` count ended the run and now gives it (`sk-base-cases.txt`).
   - Repair and home: the repair is a change of an existing declaration's type, which the batch record makes a stop (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:57`). So it goes to home 3 and a recommended row. The report must state the value, and must stop presenting `:82` as covering the `ZZ32` case of section 6.1.
4. **Four citations of the batch record are off by one**, `:18`, `:36`, `:46` and `:58`, and so are "lines 40-58" (section 0 above). `:18` is in the provenance block.
5. **The GCD/LCM citation leaves out half of what it cites.**
   - Where: `basic-integers.tex:524-525` ("If either argment is 0, the result equals the other argument") and `:528-529` ("If either argment is 1, the result equals the other argument").
   - The clash: taken alone, those two sentences give -4 for `0 GCD -4` and -5 for `1 LCM -5`. The rung asserts 4 and 5, citing `:524` and `:528` (`IntSemanticsRungI.fss:105`, `:107`), which is what the "always nonnegative" sentence on the same lines requires.
   - What is missing: the report does not say that the passage conflicts with itself for a negative argument, or that the reading is Pavol's row-334 decision.
6. **The two paths pick different methods for a mixed-width count**: `ZZ32 3 LSHIFT` a `ZZ64` count of 33 is 0 under `walk` and 25769803776 compiled (`SkCountType.*.txt`). After rung B the compiled answer stays 25769803776, because `ZZ64`'s 64-bit shift of 3 by 33 is unchanged. The batch's agreement covers only same-type counts. Outside this rung.
7. **The compiled `ZZ64` multiply rejects a product equal to `Long.MIN_VALUE`.** `longOverflowingMul` (`simpleLongArith.java:70-85`) tests `Long.MAX_VALUE / |a| < |b|` (`:82`). Through `REM` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:597`), which the compiled `MOD` and `GCD` call, `MIN REM 2`, `MIN MOD 2` and `MIN GCD 2` therefore throw (`SkMulMin.compiled.txt:2-7`). This is not the zero guard of the siblings paragraph, and no ledger row names it (`grep -n longOverflowingMul explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` is empty). Outside this rung.
8. **The spec's `shift` exists only under `walk`**: compiled, `shift(3, 33)` is `Variable shift is not defined.`, and `shift` stays bindable (`SkShiftCall.*.txt`, `SkShiftLocal.*.txt`, `SkShiftParam.*.txt`). This was decided in `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:29`, and the judge reported it to Pavol (`JUDGE.md:84`), but no ledger row carries it.

## Required corrections for the repair round

1. Finding 1, with the discipline:
   - Capture the red first (the assertion `:93` already exists; `probes/skeptic/test-default-heap.txt` is the red on the landed tree).

2. Finding 2, either way:

   - Or add an `XXX` file, shown red on a deliberate fix, and keep row 334 open for ℤ. This is home 2.

   Correct `REPORT.md:128`'s site count to name `BigNum$Lcm`.
3. Finding 3: state in `REPORT.md` section 6.1 and in `record.md` FACTS line 2 what a `ZZ32` receiver now answers for a `ZZ`, `NN32` or `NN64` count (the `ZZ64` method's 64-bit answer, typed `ZZ64`; `3 LSHIFT big(33)` = 25769803776). Name the declaration that routes it (`FortressLibrary.fss:688-691` against `:756-759` and `:637-638`) and why the rung cannot repair it (the stop at `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:57`). Point at `probes/skeptic/SkWalkOnly.walk.txt` and the recommended row.
4. Finding 4: `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:18` → `:17` in the provenance block; `:36` → `:35`, `:46` → `:45` and `:58` → `:57` in the body; "lines 40-58" → "39-57".

Finding 5: one sentence in the provenance `spec:` line and in section 4.2 saying that `basic-integers.tex:524-525` and `:528-529` also say "the result equals the other argument", which conflicts with "always nonnegative" for a negative argument, and that the rung follows the nonnegative reading as Pavol decided for row 334.

508:
509:Exponentiation of an integer to a nonnegative integer power produces an integer result.
510:If the \VAR{power} is \EXP{0}, then the result is always \EXP{1}, even if the base is \EXP{0}
511:(this definition is somewhat arbitrary but is computationally useful).
512:
513:%%  property FORALL(x, y:NN) x^y = x^(|\ y/2 /|) x^(|/ y/2 \|)
514:\begin{Fortress}
515:{\tt~}\pushtabs\=\+\( \KWD{property} \forall(x, y\COLONOP\mathbb{N})\; x^{y} = x^{(\lfloor y/2 \rfloor)} x^{(\lceil y/2 \rceil)}\)\-\\\poptabs
516:\end{Fortress}
517:
518:%%   opr GCD(self, other: ZZ): NN
519:%%   opr LCM(self, other: ZZ): NN
520:\Method{\EXP{\KWD{opr} \mathord{\OPR{GCD}}(\KWD{self}, \VAR{other}\COLON \mathbb{Z})\COLON \mathbb{Z}}}
521:\Method*{\EXP{\KWD{opr} \mathord{\OPR{LCM}}(\KWD{self}, \VAR{other}\COLON \mathbb{Z})\COLON \mathbb{Z}}}
522:
523:The operator \OPR{GCD} computes the greatest common divisor of its two arguments.
524:The result is always nonnegative.  If either argment is \EXP{0}, the result
525:equals the other argument.
526:
527:The operator \OPR{LCM} computes the least common multiple of its two arguments.
528:The result is always nonnegative.  If either argment is \EXP{1}, the result
529:equals the other argument.  If either argument is \EXP{0}, the result is \EXP{0}.
530:
531:The type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}_{>}} extends the trait
532:\EXP{\TYP{PartialOrderAndMeetBoundedLattice}\llbracket\mathbb{Z}_{>},\mid,\OPR{GCD},\OPR{LCM}\rrbracket},
533:which is to say that the strictly positive integers form a partial order and lattice with
534:the ``evenly divides'' operator \EXP{\mid} as the partial order operator and
535:with \OPR{GCD} and \OPR{LCM} as the lattice operators.
150:and \EXP{/} is subtle.
151:\See{operator-precedence} for a discussion of the relative precedence of
152:these operations and how precedence may depend on the use of whitespace.
153:
154:The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
155:For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
156:Rational computations do not overflow.
157:For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
158:according to the rules of IEEE 754.

content.content:
**The siblings, which wait on a rider.** The same `a==(-a)` test, and its twin `b==(-b)`, sits in eight more methods of the same two files, ten guards in all, and four of the methods are reachable from the prelude: `longOverflowingMul` (`simpleLongArith.java:70-85`), behind `ZZ64`'s `DOT`, `CROSS` and juxtaposition (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:591`, `:593`, `:626`) and behind `REM` (`:597`), which multiplies by the quotient, so behind `MOD`, `GCD` and `LCM` too; `longSaturatingMul` (`:248-261`, `DOTCROSS` at `:595`); and `intSaturatingNeg`/`longSaturatingNeg` (`simpleIntArith.java:278-281`, `simpleLongArith.java:269-272`, unary `DOTMINUS` at `:669` and `:584`). The saturating `Div` and `Abs` on both widths are imported and used by no body. Measured on the landed tree while this record was prepared, compiled: on `ZZ64`, `0 DOT 5`, `5 DOT 0`, `0 5`, `3 REM 5`, `3 MOD 5`, `3 GCD 5`, `12 GCD 18` and `12 LCM 18` all throw `IntegerOverflow`, where `walk` gives 0, 0, 0 and the ordinary answers; `DOTMINUS 0` is 9223372036854775807 on `ZZ64` and 2147483647 on `ZZ32`; `0 DOTCROSS 5` on `ZZ64` is -9223372036854775808. `IntegralOpsRungN.fss` passes only because none of its `ZZ64` operands makes a zero factor or a zero quotient. Without the rider, the rung repairs none of them and gives them home 2 of the shared prefix: `compiler_tests/XXXIntZeroSiblings.fss` + `.test` asserting the specification's answers above (the `XXX` prefix is honoured for `.test` files at `FileTests.java:932`), and the ledger row. With the rider, the rung applies the same rule to all ten guards and the assertions go into `IntSemanticsRungB.fss` (home 1), with one trap: once the multiply tests only the minimum, a zero factor falls through to `Long.MAX_VALUE / Math.abs(a)` (`simpleLongArith.java:82`, and `:258` in the saturating twin) and divides by zero, so zero needs its own line, or the method becomes `Math.multiplyExact`, which is Java 8 and the JVM's own spelling of exactly this check.

**What it closes, and where it stops.** Ledger: row 334 closed; rows 335 and 346 closed for the interpreter half; row 347 appended (the `narrow` caller of `Int.rc` is gone, the two exponentiation callers stay, and the row stays open); row 336 appended if the rung confirms that the `LCM` route is all it changes there. Ladder: nothing declared; the ladder stage runs the compiled path, which this rung does not touch. Checker count: 103 declared and unchanged: the one edit the stage reads is the `shift` declaration in `trait ZZ`, which adds a declaration and changes no existing type, and the `FortressLibrary` api already stops at its first kind of error (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:268-272`); the rung captures the stage's table before and after its edit as a check, not as its test, and names the total. `writesState` is false. The rung stops rather than widens if a fix would change the type of an existing declaration, or if the catchable throw cannot be had without changing how the interpreter maps Java exceptions in general.

**The gated assertions it reverses.** Rung W's assertions of the throw, `library_tests/IntConversionsRungW.fss:61-63` (`ZZ64` narrow of 2^32, MAX and MIN overflow) and `:81-82` (`NN64` narrow of 2^64-1 and 2^63 overflow), become the low-32-bit answers 0, -1, 0 and 4294967295, 0. This is the only place in the batch where a rung changes what a gated test asserts, and it is Pavol's decision, not the rung's; the `shouldOverflow` helpers there go if nothing else uses them, and nothing else in that file changes. No declaration goes into the compiler prelude (`coordinator/library-route-judgement.md`, step 0), so the spec's `shift` is declared only in the one library, by rung I; the compiled `ZZ`'s `<<<` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:547`, over `BigInteger.shiftLeft`) already computes it.

Ledger. New rows are numbered provisionally from 378 (the ledger's highest row is 377); the gather assigns final numbers in manifest order, B then I. Closed with "fixed \<commit\>" appended: 333 (B), 334 (I), 335 and 346 (each rung its half; closed when both land). Appended: 347 (I), and 336 if I confirms it. Opened: the siblings row (B).

Export statements specify the APIs that a component exports.
One important restriction on components is that no \apiN\ may be both
imported and exported by the same component. This restriction helps to
avoid some (but not all) accidental cyclic dependencies.

Every component implicitly imports the Fortress core APIs;
every fortress has at least one component implementing all of these \apisN.
A \emph{preferred} component exporting these \apisN\ (configurable by the user)
is implicitly linked to
----
(i.e., not just the declaration itself).
For example,
the reach of any top-level declaration
(including any imported declaration)
is the component containing (or importing) that declaration;
the reach of a field declaration
is the enclosing object declaration or expression;
----
We omit the name and the namespace when they are clear from context.
We say that the second declaration \emph{is shadowed by} the first 
at any point in the program that their reaches overlap.
No other shadowing is permitted in a Fortress program.

---

%%   shift(self, k: IndexInt): ZZ
\Method{\EXP{\VAR{shift}(\KWD{self}, k\COLON \TYP{IndexInt})\COLON \mathbb{Z}}}

The result of \EXP{\VAR{shift}(x,k)} is \EXP{\lfloor x \cdot 2^k \rfloor}.
This corresponds to what is sometimes called an ``arithmetic shift''
on the two's-complement representation of the integer;
positive values of \VAR{k} shifts the bits to the left,
and negative values of \VAR{k} shifts the bits to the right.

input.summary:
This repair round carries out the judge's second ruling on the skeptic's refusal, working from the branch at bdb94f2a1 (clean, nothing uncommitted).

- Finding 1 (the refusal ground): reproduced the red first. Under bin/fortress's default 256m heap, the gated test ran out of memory at :93. BigNum.shiftLeft now refuses an unrepresentable left shift with u.abs().bitLength() + v > Integer.MAX_VALUE (BigNum.java:247). The check sits after the count bound, and the catch stays as a backstop. The test now prints PASS at 256m. PrecheckBoundary.txt checks the bound against the JVM: 24 boundary cases, 0 mismatches.
- Finding 2: BigNum$Lcm now returns 0 when either argument is 0 and otherwise works on magnitudes. Three assertions (IntSemanticsRungI.fss:146-148) were red before the edit and pass after.
- Finding 3 was not repaired: a ZZ32 shifted by a ZZ, NN32 or NN64 count answers 25769803776 : ZZ64. The fix changes an existing declaration's type, which the batch reserves. It is stated in REPORT 6.1 and goes to row 379 (home 3).
- Findings 4 and 5: the citations and the GCD/LCM passage are corrected.
- Findings 6, 7 and 8 get rows 380-382.
- A row of this round's own, 383: under walk, overload resolution converts a large ZZ to a decimal string while building an error message it then discards. Measured with a stack dump.
- The LCM site count is now five natives. IntLiteral.java carries a dormant copy, bound only inside FortressBuiltin.fss's commented-out block.

Harness: 1 test OK, and the 36-file subset OK. testFast and testSystem were not run. The tracked-path check is clean, and everything is pushed at d68be2587.
decisions: BigNum$Lcm repaired here, home 1, as the judge ruled. Rejected: an XXX file with row 334 left open for ZZ.

The unrepresentable ZZ shift is refused by a bit-length check before the allocation, placed after the count bound at :246 (which keeps the long sum from overflowing) with the ArithmeticException catch kept as a backstop. Rejected: translating the JVM's exception after a ~268 MB allocation, which ran out of memory at the launcher's 256m heap.

Findings 7 and 8 get verified ledger rows 381 and 382, not XXX files. That is the shared prefix's fourth case: the specification settles them, but the repair lies outside the rung. Rejected: home 2, which would put an expected-failure test on the compiled path this rung does not touch. For 381 it would also couple rungs B and I, since B's rider may take Math.multiplyExact and turn such a test red at the batch's gate.
Opened row 383 (home 3) for the overload-resolution stringify, which I measured by stack dump. Rejected: leaving it as an unrecorded observation, which the three-homes rule does not allow.
Recorded the representable-but-heap-sized shift (3 LSHIFT 2147483645 runs out of memory at 256m and returns at 4g) as a JVM memory limit, not an integer overflow. It is not asserted.

For the runs with JAVA_FLAGS unset, the caches were pointed through the FORTRESS_CACHES environment variable, not -Dfortress.caches. bin/fortress passes only JAVA_FLAGS to the JVM (bin/fortress:28-32), and ProjectProperties.java:263-264 reads the environment variable.
